brief.place: Valley of Elah, Judah, near Socoh and Azekah
brief.dress: Bronze Age military attire: bronze helmets, coats of mail (5000 shekels), bronze shin armor; Israelite shepherd's garb (simple tunic, staff, shepherd's bag, sling); no armor tested by David
brief.buildings_and_objects: weaver's beam-sized spear, bronze javelin, sword and sheath, shepherd's pouch with five smooth stones from brook, wagons, camp tents
depiction_rules: Goliath must be shown as a massive warrior (six cubits and a span tall, ~9.5 ft), heavily armored in bronze
David must be depicted as a youth, ruddy, unarmored, relying on sling and stones, not as a warrior
Yahweh is never to be depicted as a human figure; divine action shown through wind, light, or effect on events
Philistines and Israelites are distinct: Philistines in bronze armor, Israelites in simpler attire
Do not depict David with sword or armor when he strikes Goliath—only sling and stone; sword used only after to behead
The severed head of Goliath may be shown, but not in a grotesque or humiliating manner; focus on victory through divine aid
